body.translated_text: The <s>Hastavālaprakaraṇavṛtti</s> (Commentary on the Treatise on the [Open] Hand)
Homage to <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the being of gnosis (<s>jñānasattva</s>)

body.text: namaḥ trailokye vyavahāramātre sati paramarthābhimānāt tattvārthānavagāhibhiḥ sattvairvastusvabhāvavivekadvāreṇāviparyayajñānasaṃprāptaye śāstraracaneyaṃ //
body.translated_text: Since in the three worlds only conventional practice (<s>vyavahāramātra</s>) exists, yet beings who do not grasp the meaning of reality (<s>tattvārtha</s>) cling to the [claim of] ultimate [existence] (<s>paramārthābhimāna</s>), this treatise has been composed so that, through the gateway of distinguishing the intrinsic nature of things (<s>vastusvabhāvaviveka</s>), [beings] may attain non-erroneous knowledge (<s>aviparyayajñāna</s>).

children.translated_text: The mental superimposition of a snake on a rope, upon seeing the rope, is pointless;

children.text: tadaṃśān vīkṣya tatrāpi bhrāntā buddhirahāviva // Hvpv_1 (6) //
children.translated_text: even upon examining its parts [one finds] only the same [illusion] — an understanding gone astray, like the illusion of water [in a desert]. // Hvpv_1 (6) //
All things, upon careful examination, [reveal that their] dependent bases (<s>āśritavastūni</s>) have no inherent nature (<s>svarūpa</s>);
inasmuch as they depend on something other [than themselves], they are within the range of conventional knowledge (<s>saṃvṛtijñānagocara</s>). // Hvpv_2 (24) //
Even the atom, because [the parts of] partless [entities] are inconceivable (<s>acintyatva</s>), is equal to what has no [real] existence (<s>avastu</s>);

children.text: bhrāntamatramataḥ prājñair na cintyaṃ paramārthataḥ // Hvpv_3 (45) //
children.translated_text: therefore, on the ultimate level (<s>paramārthatas</s>), the wise (<s>prājña</s>) need not think [about it] — [for it is] only an illusion (<s>bhrāntamātra</s>). // Hvpv_3 (45) //

children.text: bhrāntaṃ tadapya samyaktvad yathā bhanaṃ tathāsti na /
children.translated_text: That too is an illusion (<s>bhrānta</s>), because it is not as it appears — [things are] not [really] as they seem to be;
what appears pointlessly (<s>anarthakam bhāsamānam</s>) would be of the same nature as what resembles it [i.e., it is like seeing one thing as another]. // Hvpv_4 //
Everything that is dependent (<s>āśrita</s>), to one who knows it with a subtle intellect (<s>sūkṣmabuddhi</s>),

children.text: tyajet sa buddhiman suṣthurāgādyahibhayaṃ yathā // Hvpv_5 //
children.translated_text: the wise one (<s>buddhimān</s>) should abandon entirely — just as [one abandons] the fear of a snake [that proved to be] a rope. // Hvpv_5 //
In investigations of worldly matters (<s>laukikārthavicāreṣu</s>), one should follow worldly convention (<s>lokasiddhi</s>);

children.text: kleśan sarvasaṃ tyaktumana yateta paramārthataḥ // Hvpv_6 //
children.translated_text: on the ultimate level (<s>paramārthatas</s>), one should strive with undivided mind to abandon all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). // Hvpv_6 //
